history.sg_progress: The Administration already prioritizes the deployment of troops in missions based on requirements to protect civilians when demanded by the mandate, and all uniformed components have the responsibility to support the protection of civilians. Deployments are regularly reviewed based on changes in mandate and operational requirements. The Administration acknowledges that there may be a time lag in some reviews and redeployments, and it will seek to reduce such instances in cooperation with missions. In the specific case mentioned by the Board, which concerned a limited number of troops in one mission, required in the capital for the duration of the electoral process, MONUSCO reconfigured its footprint. The major part of the infantry battalion (300 personnel) previously deployed in Kinshasa is being redeployed to the Kasai region. The remaining troops will continue to provide security and protection for the United Nations presence in the capital.

history.administration_response: The Administration stated that it prioritized the deployments of troops in missions based on requirements to protect civilians when demanded by the mandate, while ensuring operational sustainability. Deployments are regularly reviewed on the basis of changes to the mandate and operational requirements. While stymied by the COVID-19 pandemic, the Administration continued its efforts to reduce any time lag in reviews and redeployments, and to support missions in reducing the duration of such rare instances. The specific case mentioned by the Board concerned a limited number of troops in one mission, and was resolved, as communicated in the report of the Secretary-General on the implementation of the recommendations of the Board (A/74/709). The Administration considers this recommendation implemented. 18 November 2020.

history.entities_raw: Department of Peace Operations and United Nations Multidimensional Integrated Stabilization Mission in the Central African Republic
history.sg_progress: The Administration remains concerned about the formulation of this recommendation as it appears to have no specific, measurable and time-bound criteria for its closure. Just as troop deployments are not the only strategic element in the protection of civilians, as has been shown in many years of policy and practice and has been recognized by Member States, patrols are not the only activity by missions that ultimately contribute to the protection of civilians. The Board has not demonstrated the criteria used for its assertion that there were not enough patrols by MINUSCA to protect civilians. The Administration also notes that troops were not underemployed and were used for numerous additional missions, such as convoy escorts, static security missions (the protection of United Nations sites), as well as combat missions. Recent events in the Central African Republic have demonstrated that the operations and activities of uniformed components cannot be dictated simply by the planned outputs in the results-based budgeting framework, as circumstances require operational changes in deployment, posture and activities that will impact the number of anticipated activities, including patrols. Despite travel constraints due to the COVID-19 pandemic, the Department of Peace Operations worked remotely with missions to maintain accurate assessments of the capabilities and capacities of military components and to consider various reconfigurations, including quick reaction and mobility capabilities, the ability to function in relation to the operational environment and the ability to plan and execute all types of military operations in support of the mandate. In the specific case of MINUSCA, the realignment is focused on enhancing the Mission’s capacity for the protection of civilians and its reaction capability. Operational capability has been further developed by introducing more mobile methods of operation, with a reduction in the number of positions and the generation of more mobile patrols and quick reaction capacity. The Administration considers this recommendation to be implemented and requests its closure by the Board.
